proposals: The Ministry of Finance should publish each year, beside the 41% devolution share, cesses and surcharges as a share of gross tax revenue and the resulting effective share of gross revenue transferred to states, so that the 29–30% figure in public debate is an official number.

The GST Council should commission and publish a state-by-state estimate of VAT revenue displaced by ethanol blending at current blend levels, so that modelled national figures of ₹17,865 crore at E20 and ₹26,792 crore at E30 can be checked against treasury data.

GSTN should publish an annual table of each state’s effective GST share — SGST plus settled IGST — in the same format every year, so that devolution-to-collection ratios like those in this post do not have to be recomputed from scattered releases.

The Finance Commission should publish, in its report, each state’s devolution-to-collection ratio under its chosen formula and under a GSDP-weighted alternative, so that claims such as Karnataka’s share rising from about 3.64% to 5.24% can be checked against the Commission’s own arithmetic.
